title: EPAM & Anthropic Team Up to Build the Future of Enterprise Transformation with Safe, Applied AI
pub: PR Newswire (issued by EPAM Systems, Inc.)
author: EPAM Systems · Inc.

dom.t: AI services: Deployment gaps create consulting opportunity

mo.t: AI services: Deployment gaps create consulting opportunity
Model providers: Suppliers now compete for workflows

kp.k: Partnership targets enterprise workflow automation and legacy transformation
kp.d: In its May 6, 2026 press release, EPAM announces a strategic, multi-year partnership with Anthropic combining engineering services with Claude models, Claude Code and Claude Agent SDK. EPAM presents legacy-operation simplification, workflow automation, large-scale data analysis and operational efficiency as intended client benefits, rather than reporting measured implementation results. These claims concern enterprise transformation generally, not legal services specifically.
qs: today announced a strategic, multi-year partnership with Anthropic to accelerate the delivery of safe, reliable and enterprise-grade AI.

The partnership offers clients a trusted path to simplify complex legacy operations, automate workflows, analyze large-scale datasets and improve overall operational efficiency with EPAM's proven engineering excellence and Anthropic's industry-leading Claude models, Claude Code and Claude Agent SDK.

kp.k: Large-scale certification underpins a dedicated AI engineering practice
kp.d: EPAM describes a CEO-mandated workforce-development program targeting more than 10,000 Claude-certified architects, including 250 specialized, forward-deployed engineer Black Belts. It reports over 1,300 architects already certified and more than 20,000 employees having undertaken Anthropic Academy training. The release distinguishes these reported achievements from a target of 5,000 certified architects by the end of Q3 and thousands more in 2027; Anthropic's Phil Samenuk separately describes scaling toward 10,000 certified architects.
qs: As part of a CEO-mandated program, EPAM is developing a dedicated practice of more than 10,000 Claude-certified architects, including 250 specialized, forward-deployed engineer Black Belts.
To date, over 1,300 architects have already been certified, with 5,000 to be certified by the end of Q3 and thousands more in 2027.
In addition, more than 20,000 EPAMers have successfully undertaken training via the Anthropic Academy.

kp.k: Autonomous enterprise AI increases demand for engineering service providers
kp.d: EPAM asserts that enterprises establishing foundations for enterprise-wide autonomous AI have increased demand for service providers with complex engineering expertise. It identifies engineering methodologies, delivery capabilities, applied AI expertise and agentic tools as the combination enabling movement from experimentation to AI-native operations. The claimed market advantage and sustainable growth are anticipated benefits; the release supplies no demand figures or client outcome measurements.
qs: As businesses work rapidly to establish a foundation for enterprise-wide, autonomous AI across several fronts, demand for service providers with complex engineering expertise has grown.

EPAM's trusted engineering methodologies, proven delivery approach and applied AI practice, combined with Anthropic's cutting-edge models and agentic tools, offers clients a powerful pathway to unlocking innovative AI-native solutions and moving from experimentation to a truly AI-native enterprise — establishing a distinct market advantage that drives sustainable growth.

kp.k: Service-provider repositioning links AI-native builds with safety controls
kp.d: EPAM Chief Strategy & Transformation Officer Elaina Shekhter frames the partnership as part of EPAM's ambition to become the leading AI-native strategic service provider to Global 2000 clients. She describes engineering AI-native applications and reconciling technological speed and complexity with necessary safety controls as the provider's strategic role. This is an executive statement of direction, not evidence of achieved leadership or demonstrated safety performance.
qs: Our partnership with Anthropic is an important milestone in EPAM's mission to become the leading AI-native strategic service provider to our Global 2000 clients,

As companies take on the challenge of transforming their businesses with AI, we look forward to working closely with Anthropic to shape the digital landscape and set new standards for how enterprises bridge technological speed and complexity with the necessary safety controls to create sustainable value.

kp.k: Anthropic frames partnership around production deployment and operational resilience
kp.d: Anthropic Head of Partnerships Phil Samenuk characterizes EPAM as an Anthropic services partner and says the collaboration helps enterprises move AI from concept into production. His statement includes Claude Security alongside Claude, Claude Code and the Agent SDK, and associates deployment with operational resilience and business objectives without quantifying results.
qs: We're excited to welcome EPAM as an Anthropic services partner.

Together, we're helping enterprises strengthen operational resilience and meet their business objectives by taking AI from concept to production across Claude, Claude Code, Claude Security, and our Agent SDK,

kp.k: Forward-looking claims remain conditional on adoption and business risks
kp.d: EPAM explicitly qualifies its estimates and forward-looking statements as subject to risks, uncertainties and assumptions. Among the stated contingencies are AI adoption and implementation by EPAM and its clients, alongside geopolitical and economic conditions affecting demand, revenues, operations, access to capital and profitability.
qs: Our estimates and forward-looking statements are mainly based on our current expectations and estimates of future events and trends, which affect or may affect our business and operations.

the adoption and implementation of artificial intelligence technologies by EPAM and its clients, and the effect that these events may have on client demand and our revenues, operations, access to capital, and profitability.

Although we believe that these estimates and forward-looking statements are based upon reasonable assumptions, they are subject to several risks and uncertainties and are made based on information currently available to us.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: EPAM claims its partnership with Anthropic will accelerate enterprise AI deployment, automate operations and help businesses move from experimentation to enterprise-wide AI adoption.
pts.d: This is a cross-domain source about enterprise technology and engineering services, not legal services. In its company-issued press release, EPAM presents the combination of its engineering capabilities and Anthropic's models and agentic tools as a means to simplify legacy operations, automate workflows, analyze datasets and improve efficiency. It also claims that enterprises' pursuit of autonomous AI has increased demand for technically sophisticated service providers, and that AI-native solutions can confer competitive advantage and sustainable growth. EPAM executive Elaina Shekhter describes an ambition to become the leading AI-native strategic service provider to Global 2000 clients, rather than reporting that this position has already been achieved. Anthropic's Phil Samenuk says the partnership is helping enterprises move AI into production and strengthen operational resilience.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source supports its claims with reported workforce training and certification figures, engineering experience and partner-executive statements, rather than measured client outcomes.
pts.d: EPAM reports more than 1,300 architects already certified and more than 20,000 employees trained through Anthropic Academy. These are indicators of implementation capacity, not measurements of operational savings, safety, reliability or competitive advantage. Shekhter invokes over 30 years of enterprise application and solution-building experience. Samenuk also cites the workforce training and planned certification scale. The release refers generally to industry benchmarks and analyst recognition but identifies no specific benchmark results, client cases, demand statistics or quantified productivity outcomes supporting its transformation claims.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The partnership is announced on May 6, 2026 as a multi-year initiative, with specific workforce milestones but no dated client-outcome targets.
pts.d: EPAM says it is developing a practice of more than 10,000 Claude-certified architects, including 250 specialized forward-deployed engineer Black Belts. It targets 5,000 certified architects by the end of Q3, implicitly Q3 2026 given the release date, and thousands more in 2027; it does not give a precise completion date for the full practice. Claimed enterprise benefits depend on combining engineering delivery capabilities with Anthropic tools and appropriate safety controls. There is no specified deadline or numerical target for efficiency, resilience or growth improvements. The forward-looking-statement notice qualifies expectations as subject to risks, uncertainties and assumptions, explicitly including AI adoption and implementation by EPAM and its clients.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The identified beneficiaries and affected groups are enterprise clients, engineering service providers and EPAM's technical workforce.
pts.d: Global 2000 enterprises are the principal client segment in Shekhter's statement; the company description also includes ambitious startups. Clients are promised simpler operations, workflow automation, improved efficiency and resilience, and support for production-scale AI. Engineering service providers are described as facing increased demand for complex implementation expertise. EPAM employees are affected through large-scale Claude training, certification and specialized deployment roles. The release describes workforce capability development, not job displacement or headcount reduction. It makes no specific claims about lawyers, law firms, legal departments or access to justice.
